item.title: 数万名移民进入西班牙休达领土后自愿离开
item.description:
CEUTA, Spain (AP) — Tens of thousands of migrants who crossed into Spain’stiny Ceuta territoryreturned voluntarilyto Moroccoon Friday, a day after the influx triggered chaos in theNorth Africancity and reignitedthe immigration debatein Europe and beyond. At least 57 migrants died on the journey.
Ceuta’s president put the number of migrants at 60,000, which was equivalent to 70% of the territory’s population. But most of them soon went back, the Spanish government said, after thesudden arrival of so many peoplesparked a humanitarian crisis.
Some migrants swam several miles through the sea and faced down authorities who tried to turn them back with water cannons, tear gas and warning shots. Those who died included some who drowned or were killed in a stampede to cross a breakwater barrier near a border checkpoint.
Spain deployed its armed forces and additional police to restore order in Ceuta, which sits on theStrait of Gibraltarat the entrance to the Mediterranean Sea and has been a Spanish possession since 1580. On the Moroccan side of the border, security forces clashed with migrants. The chaos also had ripple effects abroad, with Italy and France pledging to tighten their controls on people arriving from Spain.
A migrant runs from Spanish police officers as they cordon off access to the beach for people crossing from Morocco into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta, Friday, July 31, 2026. (AP Photo/Antonio Sempere)
“The situation that Ceuta is going through is absolutely unsustainable,” Ceuta President Juan Jesús Vivas told journalists.
Meanwhile, migrants from Morocco also attempted to cross into Melilla, Spain’s other territory at the tip of North Africa, where they clashed with police.
SpanishPrime Minister Pedro Sánchezvisited Ceuta on Friday and condemned the border breach, which he described as “a violation of Spain’s territorial integrity.”
Sánchez blamed human smugglers for the crisis, saying they “deceive so many young people and ultimately lead many of them to their deaths,” whether in the ocean or in the city.
The Spanish Interior Ministry released its own figures shortly after Vivas spoke, estimating that some 50,000 people had crossed from Morocco since Thursday. It added that 48,300 had already returned to Morocco by Friday evening, with hundreds more going back by the hour.
Rachid Sbihi, who leads a local workers association representing Civil Guard officers, described the situation as a “serious humanitarian crisis,” saying thousands of migrants, including unaccompanied children, were left sleeping in parks and on sidewalks, while others roamed the streets aimlessly.
The Moroccan Interior Ministry did not respond to a request for comment on the migrant figures released by the Spanish authorities.
European CommissionPresidentUrsula von der Leyensaid the images from Ceuta were “unacceptable.”
“We cannot allow anyone to come to our Union without abiding by our rules,” she said Friday in an online statement. “Dangerous crossings must stop immediately. Smuggling networks must be dismantled. And returns must be swift, as our rules allow.”
Migrants rest outside the Temporary Center for Immigrants (CETI) after crossing from Morocco into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta, Friday, July 31, 2026. CETI is the Spanish acronym for the migrant reception center. (AP Photo/Antonio Sempere)
Some of the 57 people who died had drowned, Sbihi said, but some were also killed in a stampede to cross the breakwater fence at Tarajal Beach, an urban beach near a border checkpoint with Morocco. The waters near the border fence were littered with buoys, shoes and other abandoned belongings.
Manyyoung Moroccanswho crossed into Ceuta told The Associated Press that they had hoped to find better work opportunities in Spain but were returning given the mayhem in Ceuta.
“There’s nothing at home. I’d have to work 12-hour shifts for a meager wage. That’s why I came here,” said 21-year-old Abdulah Buji, who hails from the city of Tetouan. “But I haven’t found any opportunities here either, so I have to go back.”
Moroccan police used water cannons and fired warning shots into the air to prevent migrants from crossing into Ceuta, according to rights groups in Morocco.
Morocco’s ambassador to Spain said the situation in Ceuta had unfolded against Morocco’s wishes.
“We have always prioritized legal, orderly and safe migration for all,” Karima Benyaich said. She did not comment on what prompted the migrants to cross into Ceuta.
To reach Ceuta, on the northern African coast, migrants often swim from the Moroccan town of Fnideq, covering about 3 miles (5 kilometers) to reach Spanish territory. Others attempt the crossing from the nearby town of Belyounech, where the distance is shorter.
Migrants return to Morocco from the Spanish enclave of Ceuta, Friday, July 31, 2026. (AP Photo/Antonio Sempere)
Authorities in Ceuta and Madrid have linked the border surge to a recent decision by the Spanish Supreme Court, which ruled that migrants arriving by sea could not be summarily deported, unlike those who cross by land or climb the border fence.
Sánchez said migrant smugglers misinterpreted the ruling.
The interpretation of the Supreme Court’s ruling “spread like wildfire over the past few hours through the networks of human trafficking organizations,” triggering the surge, Sánchez said.
Sánchez hasbucked the anti-migration trendthat has gained ground across Europe and in the U.S.
Earlier this year, his government moved to give residency and work permits to hundreds of thousands of migrants already living in the country without permission.
Sánchez, a Socialist, argued that it would be good for the economy and the demographics of an aging Spain. Migrants who entered irregularly after Jan. 1 this year were not included.
His critics jumped at the opportunity to attack his policy, saying it encouraged more migrants to come.
“Sánchez allows Spain to be invaded through Ceuta,” Spanish conservative politician Isabel Díaz Ayuso wrote on X.
The U.S. expressed its support for “the people of Spain, and all Europeans, against this egregious violation of their sovereignty and human rights.”
In a post on X, the State Department added that “this unacceptable incident is the direct result of the Spanish Government’s deliberate efforts to enable and facilitate mass illegal migration into Europe.”
Sánchez on Friday defendedhis migration policyand distanced it from the events in Ceuta.
In the tumult, Italy temporarily suspended its open-border Schengen agreement with Spain, reimposing border controls for air and sea. The Interior Ministry said the decision amounted to a “closure” of the borders, but experts said it was merely a resumption of border controls. The agreement allows travelers to fly between the two countries without presenting passports.
French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said France would also strengthen border checks with Spain.
The crisis in Ceuta “has nothing to do withthe regularization of migrantsadopted by the Government of Spain, as is being falsely claimed by some,” the Spanish government said in a statement late Thursday after Meloni’s announcement.
Belongings left behind by migrants float in the sea after they crossed from Morocco into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta, Friday, July 31, 2026. (AP Photo/Antonio Sempere)
Migrants from Morocco also attempted to cross into Melilla, the other Spanish territory at the tip of North Africa.
There was widespread chaos in Bni Nsar, the Moroccan town bordering the Spanish territory, where migrants clashed with police, throwing rocks and setting police vehicles ablaze, according to local media and rights groups. They reported injuries among security forces and the arrest of dozens of people attempting to cross.
Like Ceuta, Melilla is a self-governing Spanish city. Many Moroccans consider both cities to be occupied territory.
Naishadham reported from Madrid. Brito reported from Barcelona, Spain. Associated Press journalists Joseph Wilson in Barcelona, Spain; Akram Oubachir in Casablanca, Morocco; and Antonio Sempere in Ceuta, Spain, contributed.

item.title: 奥普拉·温弗瑞表示她明年将关闭南非的女子学校
item.description:
约翰内斯堡（美联社）——奥普拉·温弗瑞表示，她将在明年年底关闭她二十年前在南非为贫困女孩设立的学校。
受到与南非前总统纳尔逊·曼德拉关于教育女孩的变革力量的对话的启发，温弗瑞于 2007 年开设了奥普拉·温弗瑞女子领导力学院。他是学校开幕式的嘉宾之一。
该学院表示，温弗瑞的慈善基金会负责运营并资助这所学校，但约翰内斯堡附近的学院校园最终移交给省教育部门始终是协议的一部分。
“The dream was never simply to build a school,” Winfrey said in a statement issued by the academy on Wednesday.“这是为了投资年轻女性的无限潜力。这一使命并不仅仅限于一个校园。它继续存在于每一个可以通过教育改变未来的女孩身上。”
该学院表示，温弗瑞将通过扩大国家奖学金计划继续致力于教育南非女孩，以支持全国领先学校中具有学术才华的女孩。
据奥普拉·温弗瑞慈善基金会称，已有 500 多名女孩从该学院毕业，其中一些女孩进入了南非、美国和欧洲的顶尖大学。
豪登省政府将接管占地 52 英亩的学院校园，该校园设有 21 间教室、6 个科学和计算机实验室、一个藏书 10,000 册的图书馆和一个 600 个座位的剧院。它没有立即透露该房产的计划是什么。
豪登省教育部长Lebogang Maile表示，目前在学校就读的学生将能够在不间断的财政支持下完成学业。
该学院于 2007 年开学后不久就引起了国际关注，当时几名学生指控一名宿舍管理员对他们进行身体虐待和性虐待。
温弗瑞前往南非会见学生和家长，公开道歉，并委托进行独立调查。
2010年，这位女护士的刑事指控被无罪释放。
该报告已更正，以显示奥普拉·温弗瑞周三而非周四发表的声明。

item.title: 巴基斯坦救援人员找到布洛阿特峰雪崩后失踪的10名登山者的3具尸体
item.description:
伊斯兰堡（美联社）——官员称，巴基斯坦布洛阿特峰发生雪崩后，救援人员正在寻找 10 名失踪登山者，发现了四具尸体，并找到了其中三人，尽管恶劣天气阻碍了直升机飞行，但救援人员仍在继续寻找其他失踪登山者。
吉尔特-巴尔蒂斯坦地区政府发表声明称，找到的三具尸体分别是尼泊尔登山者 Pur Bahadur Gurung、阿曼登山者 Nathira Ahmed 和美国登山者 Mallory Geis。据称，尸体已被送往医院。
官员们表示，尽管天气恶劣，搜索小组仍找到了四名登山者的遗体，数小时后宣布了这一消息。这些官员要求匿名，因为他们无权接受媒体采访。他们没有立即确认所发现的第四具尸体的身份。
吉尔吉特-巴尔蒂斯坦地区首席部长阿姆贾德·侯赛因发表声明称，周五恶劣天气继续阻碍救援工作。
巴基斯坦阿尔卑斯山俱乐部副主席卡拉·海德里 (Karrar Haidri) 表示，登山者在尝试攀登布洛阿特峰时，遭遇雪崩，与大本营失去了联系。海德里说：“自周四以来，该小组一直失去联系。”他补充说，军用直升机参与了搜救行动。
当局表示，对失踪登山者的搜寻工作一直持续到周五晚上，并将于周六恢复。
据阿尔卑斯山俱乐部称，除了阿曼和美国登山者之外，此次探险队还包括五名尼泊尔登山者，以及巴基斯坦登山者Sohail Sakhi、一名中国登山者王和另一名外国登山者。
周五，中国政府表示正在努力核实失踪的 10 名登山者中是否有中国公民。
中国外交部发言人毛宁周五在北京表示：“我们将为有需要的中国公民提供帮助，也愿意根据巴方的需要提供帮助。”
探险队领队是著名登山家尼尔马尔·普贾 (Nirmal Purja)，他出生于尼泊尔，曾在英国军队服役，绰号“尼姆斯·戴”(Nims Dai)。2019 年，他在创纪录的 189 天里攀登了世界 14 座最高峰，这一成就出现在 Netflix 纪录片《14 个山峰：没有什么是不可能的》中。他的纪录于 2023 年被打破。
巴基斯坦旅游公司Moving Mountains上个月末宣布，探险队正在前往阿斯科尔小镇的途中，并祝愿他们攀登布洛阿特峰旅途顺利。该公司表示，这是 Geis 在巴基斯坦首次尝试 8000 米山峰，而预计这将是 Sakhi 的最后一次尝试。
据 Moving Mountains 网站称，萨基是该公司的一名导游，同时也是一名地理学家和高海拔摄影师，并曾攀登过世界上一些主要山峰。
盖斯，39 岁，住在圣安东尼奥。今年早些时候，她在社交媒体上宣布，她将关闭普拉提工作室，以“向未知领域迈出一次巨大的信念飞跃，看看生活会走向何方。我隐隐怀疑，其中会涉及到很多头盔、安全带和冰爪。”
布洛阿特峰海拔 8,047 米（26,401 英尺），是世界第 12 高山。它位于巴基斯坦的喀喇昆仑山脉，世界上 14 座 8000 米以上的山峰中有 5 座位于这里，吸引了来自世界各地的登山者。
由于雪崩和天气瞬息万变，巴基斯坦北部的登山探险中事故很常见。
汗从巴基斯坦白沙瓦报道。美联社驻北京记者 E. Eduardo Castillo 和驻西雅图记者 Hallie Golden 对本报道作出了贡献。

item.title: 美国以“未经授权旅行”为由终止一名被驱逐到墨西哥的 3 个孩子的母亲的 DACA 身份
item.description:
得克萨斯州麦卡伦（美联社）——一名得克萨斯州母亲尽管在孩童时期就获得了在美国居留的合法许可，但仍被驱逐到墨西哥。联邦政府通知她，由于她被驱逐出境而导致“未经授权的旅行”，因此将终止她的许可，她对联邦政府提起诉讼。
34 岁的杰西卡·特雷维诺 (Jessica Treviño) 本周通过律师提起诉讼，要求联邦法官介入。
特雷维诺和她的丈夫去年 12 月被捕，当时联邦特工跟踪他们和他们的两个女儿进入德克萨斯州南部的家得宝停车场。两人都被驱逐出境，现居住在墨西哥马塔莫罗斯，德克萨斯州布朗斯维尔以南。他们的三个孩子都是美国公民，与家人一起住在靠近边境的美国一侧。
特雷维诺 7 岁时被带到美国，随后在 20 岁时获得了根据儿童入境暂缓遣返计划 (DACA) 留在美国的法律许可。DACA 于 2012 年推出，并不授予合法身份，但允许数十万儿童时期来到美国的人暂时居留并获得工作许可。
作为 DACA 受益人，她必须保持无犯罪记录，并且不得前往美国境外旅行。
她的律师大卫·罗萨斯提起了诉讼。他指出，她的身份和工作许可证最近被授权至 2027 年 4 月。
上周，美国公民及移民服务局向她发出了一份意向通知，打算终止她的身份，原因是她“于 2026 年 3 月 25 日左右未经授权出境美国”，同一天她被国土安全部驱逐出境。
国土安全部在一份声明中表示，特雷维诺的丈夫在未经许可的情况下进入该国，并在被捕时正在开车。这对夫妇的车辆与一辆没有标记的国土安全调查车辆相撞后，这对夫妇被捕。国土安全部声称她“故意接受自愿离境并放弃上诉。她于 2026 年 3 月 25 日离开美国，并且不会返回。”
特雷维诺最近接受美联社采访时表示，她没有在美国移民和海关执法局拘留所签署任何表格，也不想被驱逐出境。
罗萨斯提交了一份请愿书，要求布朗斯维尔的联邦法官宣布驱逐这名妇女是非法的，命令政府为特雷维诺返回美国提供便利，并允许她的 DACA 身份继续有效。
“政府没有合法依据将她驱逐，我们提交了这份请愿书，要求将她带回家，”她的律师补充道。
今年 2 月，司法部的一名移民法官在特雷维诺被 ICE 拘留期间向她发出了自愿离境令，但有效的 DACA 身份阻止国土安全部将她驱逐出境。
“如果能够回家，我会感到非常幸运，因为那是我现在最渴望的。我真的很绝望。我已经七个月没回家了，”特雷维诺周四说道。她的三个孩子将于下个月开始上学，他们的母亲说她很想去那里。
根据国土安全部 2 月份发给伊利诺伊州民主党参议员理查德·杜宾 (Richard J. Durbin) 的一封信，现任特朗普政府已驱逐 86 名 DACA 受益人，并逮捕了另外 241 人。
DACA 受益者的倡导者表示，特雷维诺被驱逐出境是一种模式的一部分。
捍卫移民权利的政策组织 FWD.us 总裁托德·舒尔特 (Todd Schulte) 表示：“这就是在实践中蓄意、系统地摧毁 DACA 的样子：逐一针对受益人，事后编造理由，让他们的孩子在没有他们的情况下成长。”
这个故事经过修改，纠正了特雷维诺 7 岁而非 8 岁抵达美国，后来在 20 岁时获得 DACA 身份的说法。

item.title: 当局在南希·格思里 (Nancy Guthrie) 案件中提前发布了赎金字条，希望有人认出它
item.description:
PHOENIX (AP) — Authorities released an early ransom note in the investigation into thedisappearance of Nancy Guthriein hopes that someone will recognize the writing style. A second note, also released Friday, said Guthrie died shortly after she was kidnapped and “is buried in nature now.”
Both notes initially were sent to a Tucson television station days after the 84-year-old mother of“Today” show host Savannah Guthriewent missing from her home outside Tucson on Feb. 1. Authorities have not said whether Nancy Guthrie is still alive.
Saturday is the six-month mark since Guthrie went missing. No suspects have been arrested in her disappearance. The investigation is dogged by unanswered questions, such as how many people are believed to have taken part in her abduction and whether she was taken by someone who knew her.
In her latestvideoabout her mother’s disappearance, Savannah Guthrie said earlier this week that her family has been living an unending nightmare and pleaded with the kidnappers to “tell us where to look for her.”
The FBI in Washington did not immediately respond to questions about the ransom notes, including whether both messages sent to the Tucson station have been deemed legitimate.
In releasing the notes, the Pima County Sheriff’s Department said “we believe these distinctive linguistic characteristics may be recognizable to someone who knows or has interacted with the notes’ writer.”
Thefirst note, sent Feb. 2, said Guthrie was safe but scared and would be released unharmed once her captors received $4 million in cryptocurrency, with the ransom amount increasing if the first demand was not met.
It said Guthrie would be released within 12 hours if the payment was received. It also included a threat to kill her if the ransom wasn’t paid.
“Your mother is aware of this and her life is in your hands,” the first note read. “It is in the best interest of everyone to have this completed as soon as possible.”
Thesecond notewas sent Feb. 6 and said Guthrie died shortly after she was taken. “She is buried in nature now,” it said. “Nothing you could have done could have changed the outcome.” The note ended with an apology: “We are truly sorry.”
A collection of yellow flowers and notes sit at the home of Nancy Guthrie, the missing mother of “Today” show host Savannah Guthrie, in Tucson, Ariz., March 6, 2026. (AP Photo/Rebecca Noble, File)
The sheriff’s department said the notes reveal a distinctive pattern of word choices and provide insight into the writer’s mindset. The agency said someone who knows the notes’ writer may recognize the patterns.
Authorities similarly used a suspect’s own writings as a tool to apprehendTheodore “Ted” Kaczynski, branded the “Unabomber” by the FBI. Kaczynski, who killed three people and injured 23 others with mail bombs over a 17-year span, pressured The Washington Post, in conjunction with The New York Times, to publish his 35,000-word manifesto in 1995. Federal authorities encouraged its publication, leading Kaczynski’s brother and sister-in-law to recognize the syntax and anti-technology themes and tip off the FBI, bringing to a close the agency’s longest and costliest investigation at the time.
In a statement Friday, the sheriff’s department also appealed to people who may know something about the case, saying it may be difficult to come forward due to a personal relationship with someone involved or just for their own safety.
“We recognize relationships and loyalties change over time as do people and their perspectives,” the sheriff’s department wrote. “It is not too late to come forward.”
The sheriff’s office also said Friday that two videos recovered from Guthrie’s doorbell camera might be from two separate days and indicate an unidentified male prepared ahead of when Guthrie was taken. Authorities are seeking information on anyone who was behaving differently, changed their physical appearance, suddenly left the Tucson area, or had a noticeable or unexplained interest or disinterest in the case.
“Investigators continue to pursue every available technological and investigative lead,” the sheriff’s office said. “However, community members remain a vital resource as we seek to provide answers for Nancy’s family.”
People visit a banner for Nancy Guthrie, the missing mother of “Today” show host Savannah Guthrie, outside the KVOA Newsroom in Tucson, Ariz., on March 6, 2026. (AP Photo/Rebecca Noble, File)
The FBI had released surveillance videos of a masked person who authorities said appeared to tamper with a camera on Nancy Guthrie’s front porch and block it with a plant. They described the person as a male about 5 feet, 9 inches (1.75 meters) tall.
On Feb. 4, Savannah Guthrie and her siblings first shared avideo statementsaying they were aware of media reports of a purported ransom letter and that they were ready to talk and listen, but they wanted proof that their mother was alive. Camron Guthrie, the brother of the “Today” co-anchor, said the following day that the familyhad not heard directlyfrom whoever took their mother.
A day after the second note was sent, Savannah Guthrie said on Feb. 7 that the siblings received a message and “understand,” without sharing details. She said they were begging for their mother to be returned to them. “We will pay,” Guthrie said.
The family has continued to share their pleas for information in videos posted to social media.
Also, two men detained and released early in the investigation into Nancy Guthrie’s disappearance are seeking a combined $3 million against a southern Arizona sheriff’s department. In a legal claim, they say they were wrongfully held by law enforcement.
The claim made Thursday against Pima County Sheriff Chris Nanos’ department centers on the separate detentions of Carlos Alfredo Palazuelos and Daniel Maddow on Feb. 10. It said they were released hours later but have suffered from having been mentioned in the investigation.
Nanos’ office declined to comment on the notice of claim, a necessary precursor to filing a lawsuit against government entities.
Associated Press writer Hannah Schoenbaum in Salt Lake City contributed.

item.title: 司法部决定撤销对前奥运选手涉嫌破坏倒影池的指控
item.description:
华盛顿（美联社）——周五，司法部驳回了一项指控一名前奥运选手故意破坏林肯纪念堂倒影池的刑事案件，称检察官最近收到的证据驳斥了破坏行为是罪魁祸首的观点。
政府律师在一份长达 20 页的法庭文件中表示，自大卫·赫恩 (David Hearn) 被起诉以来，内政部提供的更多文件显示，造成损坏的原因是承包商安装不当，以及“在 2026 年独立日前后几周的美国 250 周年庆祝活动之前急于完成该项目”。此外，最近的目视检查显示整个泳池都受到了损坏，包括中间的地方——检察官表示，破坏者不太可能试图剥掉泳池的内衬。
美国检察官珍妮·皮罗 (Jeanine Pirro) 在提交的文件中表示：“鉴于所有这些新发现的信息，很难将倒影池的广泛损坏归咎于故意破坏行为，更不用说在合理怀疑范围内证实这一事实。”该文件要求法官正式驳回此案。
赫恩的律师在一份声明中表示，根本不应该对他提起诉讼。
“今天的驳回并不能消除滥用政府权力逮捕和指控一名没有做错的爱国美国人的行为。政府的做法已经准备好了，开火，瞄准。政府欠赫恩先生道歉，”律师们说。
这次解雇对司法部来说是一个尴尬的挫折，司法部曾指责检方对华盛顿地标建筑造成的损害负责，唐纳德·特朗普总统在美国建国 250 周年庆典之前启动了一项大规模翻修工程。特朗普在没有提供证据的情况下声称损坏是由破坏行为造成的。
但该案长期以来一直面临证据问题和挑战。数周以来，赫恩一直坚称自己无罪，他的支持者将此次起诉定性为特朗普政府出于政治动机试图转移责任并寻找替罪羊。
本周早些时候，赫恩的律师寻求查阅大陪审团的笔录，因为他们称这一过程存在“违规行为”。他们说，国家公园管理局的一名官员作证说，在赫恩涉嫌触碰泳池之前，该泳池就已经遭到损坏，无法量化赫恩造成的任何损坏，并表示无论他的行为如何，都需要进行相同的维修。
“证人的证词证实，在赫恩先生做出任何指控的行为之前，泳池已经存在严重损坏，需要修复，”他的律师写道。“据目击者称，泳池每周泄漏的水超过一百万加仑；其伸缩缝已超过使用寿命；内衬已出现裂口。”
赫恩本月早些时候对一项破坏财产重罪表示不认罪，并计划于 9 月 28 日在华盛顿特区高等法院开始审判。该指控指控赫恩对泳池造成至少 1,000 美元的损失，一旦定罪，最高可判处 10 年监禁。
在周五的法庭文件中，检察官表示，他们最近才收到破坏起诉依据的新信息。
“直到这些文件出示后，（检察官）才第一次意识到有信息表明，损坏是由于安装不当造成的，而不是内政部最初所代表的破坏行为。”他们写道，检察官“只能依赖”表明损坏是由破坏行为造成的初步信息。
赫恩告诉美联社，6 月 19 日，他在骑自行车时停在泳池边，之后被国民警卫队和美国公园警察拘留了五个小时。他说，他伸手检查泳池新剥落的涂层，并短暂触摸了附着在泳池一侧的一块块，但他说，他服从了一名公园工作人员的要求，让他放开它。
美国奥林匹克和残奥委员会在其网站上称，67 岁的赫恩来自马里兰州贝塞斯达，参加了三届夏季奥运会，并在 1996 年亚特兰大奥运会上获得了第九名。

item.title: 特朗普在处理西班牙移民危机时赞扬在戴维营举行的“独特”内阁会议
item.description:
CAMP DAVID, Md. (AP) — PresidentDonald Trumptook Friday’s Cabinet meeting on the road toCamp David, using the historic rustic backdrop of the presidential retreat to boast of his administration’s achievements while seizing on a migrant crisis in Spain to make his case for why voters should keep the Republican Party in power.
The Cabinet meeting, the 13th such gathering of Trump’s second term, came just three months before the November midterm elections that could serve as a check on his power if Democrats take control of one or both chambers of Congress. His warnings about Spain echoed language he used ahead of the 2018 midterms, when hewarned of caravans of migrantsheaded to the southern U.S. border.
“You know, I saw Spain yesterday, and I watched the catastrophe that took place. It looks like an invasion of a country by hundreds of thousands of people,” Trump said. “And that same thing is going to happen to us if the Republicans don’t get elected. Except worse, much bigger.”
Some 60,000 migrants crossedfrom Moroccointo Spain’stiny Ceuta territoryover the past 24 hours. Roughly half of them have already made their way back voluntarily, according to the Spanish government, but at least 57 have died on the journey.
Separately, he deflected blame for a series of cyberattacks that targeted 30 water systems in Minnesota on the state’s “grossly incompetent” Democratic leadership. Officials have not publicly identified who was behind the attacks, though the FBI, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency and other agencies warned in an advisory last week that Iranian hackers have been targeting water and wastewater systems and the operational controls of other critical infrastructure sectors.
“They blame it on Iran,” Trump said, without offering evidence. “I don’t think so. I think I blame it on Minnesota because they’re grossly incompetent.”
The president regularly convenes his Cabinet throughout his terms as a setting to promote his administration’s policies while fielding questions on the news of the day, but what made Friday’s unusual was that it was at Camp David, the government-owned retreat nestled in Maryland’s Catoctin Mountains where Trump held one Cabinet meeting during his first term.
Trump began the meeting by noting it was “something very unique.” The White House called it the first-ever televised Cabinet meeting from thepresidential retreat.
“It’s Camp David, and this room is a very, very special room,” Trump said.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth were among the Cabinet officials who spoke before Trump took questions from journalists. The public portion of the meeting ended after about an hour.
In the lengthy question-and-answer session, Trump commented on the latest developments regarding the war in Iran and adeal he announced Thursdaythat would lead to the disarmament of the Palestinian group Hamas. He also lamented that a $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund to compensate his allies was “dead” and appeared to back off a pledge he made earlier this month to grant Ukraine a license to manufacture Patriot air defense systems.
“I don’t think this would ever happen, but, you know, there’s people that, you give that technology, they can someday turn on you,” Trump added. “You look at war, that’s happened a couple of times over the years, right? So we have to be very careful.”
On the Hamas agreement, Trump acknowledged that the agreement that would also lead to Israel’s withdrawal from Gaza will have “ups and downs.” Still, he called it a “great breakthrough” that has been helped along by the U.S. and Israel’s war with Iran, which has served as Hamas’ prime backer.
Trump also remarked on the anti-weaponization fund that isholding up the confirmation of Todd Blancheas his attorney general, saying the pot of money is “dead” and that “I wish it weren’t, to be honest with you.”
The president continued to defend the people who could potentially benefit from the fund, mainly those who stormed the Capitol on Jan. 6, 2021, to stop the certification of Democrat Joe Biden’s victory over him.
“Their families have been ruined,” Trump said. Those people “wanted to go to a rally or an event and ended up spending the rest of their lives in horror.”
Trump said Blanche has been a “pawn in this whole thing.” Blanche, who was present, did not speak in the public portion of the Cabinet meeting.
The camp’s primary purpose is to provide presidents a place to rest, relax and recharge. It was established in 1942 during Franklin Roosevelt’s presidency and has been used by every president since.
Roosevelt had enjoyed relaxing aboard a presidential yacht, but the military and the U.S. Secret Service began to worry about his safety on open water during World War II. As a result, Roosevelt asked the National Park Service to find sites within 100 miles (160 kilometers) of the White House that he could use for rest.
He chose what is now known as Camp David. He gave it the original name of Shangri-La, from James Hilton’s novel “Lost Horizon.” President Dwight Eisenhower renamed it Camp David, after his grandson and father.
Trumpspent more weekends at the retreatin his first term but has visited sparingly in his second, most recently in June for Father’s Day.
In 2019, during his first term, Trump announced on social media that he had canceleda secret weekend meetingat Camp David with Taliban and Afghanistan leaders — scheduled for just days before the anniversary of the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks — after a bombing in the capital of Kabul killed a dozen people, including a U.S. soldier.
Presidents throughout history have turned to Camp David when they needed security and privacy for sensitive diplomatic talks with foreign leaders.Jimmy Cartertook the leaders of Egypt and Israel there in 1978 for talks that produced the Camp David Accords, a peace agreement between the two countries.
The 180-acre (73-hectare) retreat, which is run by the Navy and guarded by Marines, has a cabin named Aspen that’s reserved for the president, plus about a dozen other cabins for guests. A main lodge has conference rooms, a dining room and an office for the president.
Superville and Kim reported from Washington. Associated Press writers Collin Binkley, Will Weissert and Aamer Madhani contributed to this report from Washington.

item.title: 国际足联高级管理人员表示员工因因凡蒂诺的世界杯抛售计划而受到欺骗
item.description:
日内瓦（美联社）——国际足联首席运营官表示，其工作人员被主席因凡蒂诺的世界杯抛售计划所欺骗，并于周五建议该项目不得继续进行。
苏黎世高管凯文·拉穆拉尔（Kevin Lamourall）在向美联社发表的一份声明中邀请因凡蒂诺解雇他，该声明为国际足联老板将未来世界杯利润股份出售给私募股权基金的计划带来的强烈影响为他的同事们辩护。
拉莫尔写道，工作人员因因凡蒂诺近几个月来在出售计划中缺乏开放性而“欺骗”了他们，“他们应该得到比蔑视和恐吓更好的待遇”。
“这是一个人的项目，”因凡蒂诺在国际足联和欧洲足球机构欧足联的长期同事拉莫尔写道。“这个项目不仅不能继续进行……而且现在是足球政治领导人问自己正确问题并做出正确决定的时候了。”
拉莫尔发表声明的几个小时前，因凡蒂诺的高级顾问卡洛斯·科代罗（Carlos Cordeiro）辞职并敦促国际足联其他高级工作人员发表讲话。卡洛斯·科代罗是前高盛银行家，代表足球机构参加世界杯世界杯工作组。
“当国际足联考虑出售世界杯股份时，我不能袖手旁观，”科代罗在一份声明中写道。这位前美国足协主席表示，他没有参与约书亚·库什纳创建的纽约投资基金支持的计划的谈判。
“让我澄清一下。我没有参与这项提议，并且我明确反对它，”科代罗说。他称这笔价值 200 亿美元的商业子公司“对足球界来说是一笔糟糕的交易”。
拉穆尔并未辞去自 2024 年以来一直担任的职务，但表示他对同事负有责任。
这位法国官员表示：“如果这意味着我会失去工作，那就这样吧。”“我会理解并尊重这个决定。至少今晚我会睡个好觉。”
二十年前，拉莫尔作为时任欧足联主席米歇尔·普拉蒂尼的助手从政界进入足球界。他经常在足球政治中发挥国际作用，与非洲和亚洲的国际足联成员联合会联络，这些联合会正在权衡自己对因凡蒂诺在 9 月 19 日截止日期前提出的各 2000 万美元报价的决定。
近年来，科代罗经常与因凡蒂诺一起进行工作访问，在白宫会见美国总统唐纳德·特朗普。
“足球一直是我生活的核心，在银行业工作超过 35 年之后，我既了解这项资产的价值，也了解放弃部分资产的后果，”他说。“这就是为什么这个提议应该被拒绝。”
欧洲国家已同意抵制世界杯和国际足联所有其他赛事，以抗议詹尼·因凡蒂诺将私募股权投资者引入足球界最大赛事的计划。北美足球机构也拒绝了这一提议。这是您需要了解的内容。
因凡蒂诺提议将国际足联的商业业务（包括男子和女子世界杯和世俱杯）分拆为一家价值 200 亿美元的子公司，其中 20% 的股份由私人投资者持有。国际足联描述的“主要投资者”是库什纳，他是特朗普女婿贾里德·库什纳的弟弟。
“国际足联已经获得了非凡的财政资源。该组织拥有数十亿美元的储备，并且没有债务，”科代罗说。他指出，国际足联在过去四年中与刚刚结束的男子世界杯相关的收入为 150 亿美元。
“在这种背景下，出售足球最有价值资产的永久股份来筹集 42 亿美元毫无意义。这是在没有任何令人信服的理由的情况下抵押足球的未来，”他说。
科代罗表示，他与因凡蒂诺一起为国际足联工作了五年，与“敬业、有原则、深切关心这项运动的人”一起工作。
“我希望他们也能大声疾呼，”他写道，“因为如此重大的决定应该是为了足球的利益，而不是那些从中获利的人的利益。”
因凡蒂诺担任国际足联主席已经十多年了，明年三月他似乎肯定会在无人反对的情况下连任。国际足联设定了 11 月 18 日为挑战者挺身而出的最后期限。
拉穆尔是因凡蒂诺核心圈子的一员，他们为他竞选2016年2月的国际足联主席选举出人意料地获胜。

item.title: 罗莫因涉嫌酒后驾车被捕后，已从哥伦比亚广播公司体育频道休假
item.description:
托尼·罗莫（Tony Romo）上周因涉嫌酒后驾驶车辆被捕，随后他担任哥伦比亚广播公司（CBS）NFL报道首席分析师的职务已被停职。
哥伦比亚广播公司体育周五宣布，前达拉斯牛仔队四分卫正在休假，“直至另行通知”。在罗莫缺席期间，JJ 瓦特将与吉姆·南茨和特雷西·沃尔夫森一起成为哥伦比亚广播公司体育频道的 NFL 主队。
46 岁的罗莫于 7 月 23 日在威斯康星州 43 号州际公路向南行驶时被拦下被捕。根据密尔沃基县治安官办公室的报告，罗莫在被拘留、登记和释放之前在现场清醒测试中表现不佳。
哥伦比亚广播公司体育频道宣布这一消息之前，密尔沃基县治安官办公室发布的消息显示，在罗莫的黑色吉普车被拖走之前的盘点过程中，在乘客侧发现了一瓶打开的酒精饮料。
根据传票，警方在看到罗莫在一个戈尔区超车后拦下了他，该戈尔区将州际交通与从入口匝道进入的车辆分开。警方表示，罗莫在拦截过程中询问了什么是血腥区域。
本周早些时候发布的随身摄像机镜头显示，罗莫告诉警员，他来自一个高尔夫球场，正准备“去看望爷爷奶奶”，但被拦住了。一名副警长告诉罗莫，他怀疑罗莫身体有问题，因为他有“玻璃般的红色眼睛”和“令人陶醉的酒精饮料的气味”。
罗莫在距离威斯康星州伯灵顿密尔沃基约 35 英里的高中上学。
自 2017 年以来，他一直是哥伦比亚广播公司 (CBS) NFL 报道的首席比赛分析师，此前他在 2004-16 赛季的 NFL 职业生涯中四次参加职业碗比赛，并且完全在达拉斯度过。
罗莫以 248 次达阵传球，仍然是牛仔队队内的领军人物。他一直保持着队史职业传球码数纪录（34,183 码），直到上赛季达克·普雷斯科特超越他。
瓦特于 2023 年加入哥伦比亚广播公司。他曾在《今日美国橄榄球联盟》(The NFL Today) 担任分析师两个赛季，然后从上赛季开始与伊恩·伊格尔 (Ian Eagle) 合作成为该电视台的第二号人物。
预计罗莫要到 9 月 13 日常规赛开幕周日才能参加他的第一场比赛。哥伦比亚广播公司 (CBS) 将于 8 月 28 日转播辛辛那提猛虎队和费城老鹰队之间的季前赛。
哥伦比亚广播公司可能会在接下来的几周内公布常规赛前三周的比赛分配和播音员配对。

item.title: 因凡蒂诺在遭到巨大阻力后放弃了将世界杯利润出售给私募股权的计划
item.description:
日内瓦（美联社）——在遭到足球界各个角落的抵制后，国际足联主席詹尼·因凡蒂诺放弃了将世界杯利润出售给私人股本的分裂计划。
因凡蒂诺的决定是在他担任白宫小组成员的高级顾问辞职、亚洲足球机构与欧洲和北美一起反对这一决定后做出的。
因凡蒂诺在周五的一份声明中表示：“在仔细听取了所有意见后，很明显，该项目已经造成了一定程度的分歧，无论支持程度如何，都不再符合最初设定的目标。”“我们的目的一直是——也将永远是——团结和进步。因此，这个提案不会继续下去。”
因凡蒂诺曾提议创建一家价值 200 亿美元的公司，与包括库什纳家族在内的私人投资者一起运营世界杯，但自周二宣布这一消息以来，遭到了日益强烈的反对。
周四，欧足联 55 个成员国同意抵制世界杯和国际足联所有其他赛事，因为因凡蒂诺的计划。北美足协和亚洲足联也表示反对该计划。
欧足联在一份声明中表示：“有些东西太重要了，无法出售。”“国际足联世界杯属于足球。它永远都是。只要欧洲有发言权，它就永远不会被出售。”
因凡蒂诺的高级顾问卡洛斯·科代罗（Carlos Cordeiro）是前高盛银行家，代表足球机构参加世界杯世界杯特别工作组，他于周五辞职，并敦促国际足联其他高级工作人员公开表态。
“当国际足联考虑出售世界杯股份时，我不能袖手旁观，”科代罗在一份声明中表示，就在国际足联坚称“没有人出售足球”几个小时后。
几小时后，国际足联首席运营官凯文·拉穆尔向美联社发表声明称，国际足联工作人员因因凡蒂诺近几个月来在出售计划中缺乏开放性而受到欺骗，该项目不得继续下去。
“这是一个人的项目，”因凡蒂诺在国际足联和欧洲足球机构欧足联的长期同事拉莫尔写道。“这个项目不仅不能继续进行……而且现在是足球政治领导人问自己正确问题并做出正确决定的时候了。”
因凡蒂诺提议将国际足联的商业业务（包括男子和女子世界杯和世俱杯）分拆为一家价值 200 亿美元的子公司，其中 20% 的股份由私人投资者持有。
国际足联描述的“主要投资者”是一家总部位于纽约的投资公司，由美国总统唐纳德·特朗普的女婿贾里德·库什纳的弟弟约书亚·库什纳创建。
国际足联的下一场比赛是 9 月 5 日在波兰举行的 20 岁以下女子世界杯，欧足联成员表示他们将抵制该赛事。
这一失误可能会让因凡蒂诺付出高昂的代价，特别是在拉莫尔和科代罗介入之后。
因凡蒂诺在 2019 年和 2023 年均无异议连任，根据国际足联法规，他可以再连任四年。下届主席竞选的最后期限是 11 月 18 日，距离国际足联非洲总部所在地摩洛哥拉巴特投票整整四个月。

item.title: 音乐评论：爱莉安娜·格兰德的《Petal》展现了一位流行歌星最内敛的一面
item.description:
纽约（美联社）——大腕阿丽亚娜·格兰德（Ariana Grande）去世了。在《Petal》中，她的第八张录音室专辑，也是自《Wicked》结束和 2024 年的《Eternal Sunshine》结束后的首张完整专辑，这位流行巨星在 12 首真正克制的歌曲中审视自己。
主打单曲“Hate That I Made You Love Me”以其静音的接收和灵活的钩子，让人们直接感受到了即将到来的氛围转变。这首歌曲成为 Grande 第 10 个登上 Billboard Hot 100 排行榜第一名的歌曲，其特点是柔和的声音传递，充满了冒泡、琶音的合成器和轻柔流行合唱，这一切都由 Grande 和她的制作人——她自 2018 年的《Sweetener》以来一直合作的 Ilya Salmanzadeh 和瑞典谜马克斯·马丁 (Max Martin) 提供。第一次听时，感觉就像是一个考验：这位以超越竞争对手而闻名的艺术家能否完成低调的声乐表演？“我讨厌我让你爱我，”她唱道——由谁来诠释。“因为我几乎没有尝试过。”
在最棘手的时刻都有一种轻松和轻松的感觉，构成《Petal》的 12 首歌曲中的大部分都是如此。充满活力的制作在《Oh Well》中回归，分散了歌词中清晰的结束语的注意力。“美好的事物可以取代功能障碍和痴迷，”她唱道。“谢谢，但我会马上见你/祝你在通往地狱的路上好运/哦，好吧！”
这里有各种各样的纹理，而且它们比以前更酷——近乎无精打采，但仍然保留着很多魅力。
《Petal》拥有一种忧郁的 R&B 风格，这要归功于 SZA 的流畅；《Freak》的表现就像一场醒着的梦，或者也许是一场噩梦——一首带有朦胧声音配音的轻松自白。没有她标志性的表演，没有传奇般的声音时刻。格兰德已经继续前进，这是她有权做的。但她的“大感情”微妙程度足以让忠诚者保持参与吗？
更加粗俗、充满活力的 Grande 再次出现在专辑的最后也是最好的第三首，尤其是在“Like I Do”中的强劲低音之上，或者在缓慢燃烧的“Never Get Over Me”中的“Thegras is wayer greener/Since I be under ya”中。它飘进飘出，让专辑中的佼佼者“Bad Thing (Bunny Hop)”以一种迷恋的冲动击中——这正是它的预期目的，这首歌充满了梦幻流行吉他的冲击力，威肯式的推进力和胃里蝴蝶般的抒情以及她特有的创造性发音。（例如：“感觉像个青少年/我想我真的需要你。”）它导致了更接近的“Nowhere，Nobody”及其复古的声乐旋律和声码器效果。
在《Petal》的新闻材料中，格兰德将这张专辑描述为“充满生机，在寒冷、坚硬和具有挑战性的裂缝中成长的东西”。这有一定道理：在这十几首歌曲中，有一些小小的欢乐，埋藏在大气的制作和无精打采的旋律之下。但流行音乐中最具弹性的歌手也有选择控制它的自由。

item.title: FCC 主席为针对 ABC 的行动辩护，称广播公司必须“为了公共利益”运营
item.description:
联邦通信委员会主席布伦丹·卡尔周五为其机构最近针对美国广播公司的行动进行了辩护，称广播公司有责任“以公共利益为重”，而联邦通信委员会只是试图恢复这一标准。
卡尔在接受福克斯商业网络采访时表示，像美国广播公司这样的广播公司“与美国人民达成了一项协议。你们广播公司可以获得补贴，可以免费使用宝贵的公共资源，即价值数十亿美元的电视广播。作为交换，你们必须以公共利益为重。”
卡尔告诉主播玛丽亚·巴蒂罗莫：“看，作为一个国家，我们应该拥有一个值得信赖、受人尊敬的新闻媒体，但我们还没有做到这一点。”“所以我希望更多的广播公司回归到他们的公共利益义务。”
此前一天，美国广播公司在与唐纳德·特朗普总统的联邦通信委员会的不断升级的斗争中再次发起猛攻，再次指责该机构公然试图压制其受宪法保护的言论自由，进而压制美国所有媒体的言论自由。
ABC 指责该机构对其进行报复仅仅是因为它不喜欢 ABC 节目的政治内容。
该网络在向该机构提交的最新文件中发表了新评论，正式反对 FCC 于 4 月份启动的对 ABC 八个本地广播许可证到期前的早期审查。
文件称：“毫无疑问，委员会为什么要挑选这八个电台。”“每个节目都属于 ABC 旗下，政府多次公开呼吁撤销 ABC 的许可证，因为它不喜欢 ABC 网络节目所表达的内容和观点。”
“对美国广播公司的报复向该国每家媒体公司发出了一个信号，”它继续说道。“适应政府对新闻报道应该是什么样子的看法，否则就要付出代价……工具各不相同，但目标却没有变化：媒体行业太害怕官方报复而不敢自由报道新闻。”
许可证审查只是美国广播公司和美国联邦通信委员会之间长期对抗的一部分。该电视台还在与卡尔制作《The View》的努力作斗争，这是一档脱口秀节目，其主持人和嘉宾经常激怒特朗普，并遵守平等时间规则——ABC 表示，该机构本身在二十多年前就已经解决了这个问题。
这些规则要求给予竞争公职的候选人平等的通话时间。真正的新闻节目除外。FCC 在 2002 年的一项决定中认定该节目具有此类资格。
特朗普还多次呼吁解雇深夜主持人吉米·金梅尔。
当美国联邦通信委员会 (FCC) 在 4 月份对美国广播公司 (ABC) 的牌照进行早期审查时，正值美国联邦通信委员会 (FCC) 因一个冒犯特朗普的笑话而与金梅尔发生争执。然而，该机构引用了该公司的多元化、公平性和包容性做法，卡尔在福克斯采访中也提到了这些做法。
他说，为了公共利益行事，“意味着你不能歪曲新闻、广播恶作剧。你不能参与这种令人反感的 DEI 歧视形式。”他没有详细说明。
ABC 在周四提交的文件中提到了 FCC 网站上发布的超过 14 万条评论，其中超过 95% 的评论支持 ABC 的立场。
“对于许可证更新程序来说，对电视台的大量支持是前所未有的，”它说。“这些支持者跨越了意识形态范围，但都对言论自由和新闻自由有着共同的基本承诺。”
美国广播公司在其冗长的文件中还指出，联邦通信委员会要求提前申请许可证更新的情况是多么罕见。
美国广播公司表示，“直到委员会采取这一步骤的前一天，它已经有五十多年没有要求提前申请许可证续签了。”“委员会背离这些规范的行为暴露了真实情况：政府正在对美国广播公司行使其第一修正案权利进行报复。
“仅凭这一点就应该阻止这些诉讼程序的进行。”
乔斯林·诺维克 (Jocelyn Noveck) 为美联社报道媒体和娱乐的交叉领域。

item.title: Anthropic 表示其 AI 模型在测试期间黑客攻击了 3 个组织
item.description:
Anthropic 表示，其人工智能模型在测试期间入侵了另外三个组织，就在几天前，ChatGPT 制造商 OpenAI 在披露其流氓模型入侵了另一家公司后，提出了对人工智能控制的担忧。
Claude 背后的总部位于旧金山的人工智能公司 Anthropic 周四在其网站上发布消息称，该公司在审查了超过 141,000 次评估运行后发现了这三起事件。
Anthropic 表示，针对 OpenAI 事件，该公司启动了一项“大规模”网络安全审查，专门寻找其人工智能模型是否能够从本应封锁的测试环境中访问互联网的证据。
Anthropic称，事件涉及的模型为Claude Opus 4.7、Claude Mythos 5以及内部研究测试模型。该人工智能公司表示，最早的事件可以追溯到四月份。
Anthropic 表示：“克劳德使用基本技术破坏了受影响组织的基础设施，例如利用弱密码。”
在所有这三起事件中，人工智能模型的任务都是“夺旗”网络安全挑战，Anthropic 表示这是评估模型网络能力的方式之一。
报告称，这些模型被赋予了一个虚构的场景，并被告知一条秘密信息或“旗帜”已隐藏在网络上的另一台机器上，目的是闯入并检索它。
它补充说，它已经联系了受影响的组织，但没有透露具体名称。其中两人表示，他们之前没有发现这一活动。Anthropic 表示，它“正在继续接触第三个”。
Anthropic 表示，它与 Irregular 进行了审查，该实验室自称是“第一个前沿安全实验室”。
Irregular 在 X 上的一篇帖子中表示：“应对这些风险需要整个人工智能生态系统进行更密切的合作。”
上周，OpenAI 表示，其人工智能模型在对其模型进行评估时出现了异常，闯入了人工智能初创公司 Hugging Face 的服务器。OpenAI 将其描述为“重大安全事件”。
ChatGPT 制造商 OpenAI 周二表示，其人工智能系统自行入侵了另一家人工智能公司，该公司称之为“前所未有的网络事件”。
这些事件凸显了人工智能安全和控制方面的漏洞，并提出了随着人工智能技术在全球范围内的使用变得更加广泛，如何安全地将人工智能置于人类控制之下的问题。
多年来，研究人员一直在警告技术带来的风险以及更强大的人工智能防御工程的必要性。
Anthropic 周四在其网站上表示：“在模型发布之前进行安全测试，正是因为我们还不知道它的能力。”
专门从事网络安全和威胁检测的网络安全公司 NyxLab 联合创始人兼首席执行官 Kok Tin Gan 认为，未来还会发生更多此类事件。
甘说：“越来越多的问题是管理人工智能可以使用哪些代理、它们拥有哪些权限、哪些行动需要批准，以及我们如何确保它们保持在范围内。”
但他表示，人工智能安全的未来不仅仅局限于人工智能模型的安全。
甘说：“如果我们只是给人工智能一个目标，并让它决定如何实现它，那么当它采取的行动在技术上满足了目标，但超出了我们的预期范围或期望时，我们就不会感到惊讶。”
因此，加强对这些人工智能模型背后的组织和当局的治理将变得越来越重要，他说。

item.title: 美国和伊朗的战斗推高能源价格，主要石油公司获得巨额利润
item.description:
NEW YORK (AP) — American oil and gas giants raked in massive spring profits while fighting betweenIran and the U.S. impeded petroleum shipments and consumers around the world paid more for fuel and confronted shortages.
The conflict, now in its sixth month, halted most shipping through theStrait of Hormuz, a narrow waterway that previously served as a delivery route for a fifth of the world’s oil and natural gas. With global supplies constrained, prices for Brent crude, the international standard, soared from about $70 to above $100 a barrel for much of March, April and May, and at one point reached $126.
The money that oil companies accrued between the beginning of April and the end of June could receive extra scrutiny this year. Gasoline, diesel and jet fuel prices climbed sharply during that period, increasing costs for drivers and airline passengers. Supplies ran low in some countries, leading to sporadic fuel rationing in Australia and government office closures in Nepal and Sri Lanka.
Exxon Mobil on Friday reported that its second quarter profits doubled to $14.53 billion, boosted by record diesel production. The oil giant, based in Spring, Texas, brought in $116.02 billion in revenue, up 42%.
Chevron, based in Houston, nearly quadrupled its profits to $12.07 billion and revenue jumped 56% to $70.06 billion.
Six of Europe’s largest oil companies posted combined first-quarter profits of $22 billion, more than 40% higher than last year.
“There are constituencies around the world who are having a very good crisis, and the oil producers are one of them,” said Patrick Galey, fossil fuels lead at Global Witness, a nonprofit organization that investigates environmental issues. “When you compare that to the hundreds of millions of people who are struggling with rolling blackouts, with electricity curbs, rationing, waiting in line for food queues, or the disruption to fertilizers and the potential impact that that has on food prices, we don’t think that it’s a justifiable price for the rest of the world to be paying.”
Energy companies such as Exxon and Chevron do not set the price of American oil, which ricocheted from $68 to $115 a barrel during the quarter. It’s driven by supply and demand, and what traders, refiners and other buyers are willing to pay.
Nevertheless, Democrats in Congress introduced bills in March to tax major oil producers for profits they show from 2026 onward and have the tax proceeds redistributed to consumers.
“It’s fair to put a windfall profits tax on inordinate windfall profits rather than cut off children’s food programs,” Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse, a Rhode Island Democrat who introduced the Senate version of the legislation.
Whitehouse’s measure and a companion bill introduced by U.S. Rep. Ro Khanna of California would amend the U.S. tax code to impose a per-barrel tax on companies that produced or imported at least 300,000 barrels of oil per day in 2025.
“We cracked $4 again per gallon last weekend in gas stations that I drove by, and that’s a big expense, particularly for families that get their income from driving around from job to job in the work van or the work truck,” Whitehouse said.
The average price for a gallon of regular gasoline in the U.S., which was below $3 before the U.S. and Israel launched attacks on Iran, reached $4.11 Friday, about $1 more than ast year at this time.
The UK and other European countries implemented temporary windfall profits taxes on fossil fuel companies in 2022. The UK extended that to 2030, according to Tax Foundation Europe.
“Penalizing the businesses who stood by those countries and provided that product going forward is very short-sighted,” Exxon CEO Darren Woods said in a call with investors Friday. “We canceled investments that we had planned for Europe based on the last time they passed a windfall profits tax.”
Outfits such as Exxon and Chevron, which also own refineries, are in the best position to profit from the current market conditions, said Tom Seng, assistant professor of energy finance at Texas Christian University.
Refineries turn oil into gasoline, diesel, jet fuel and home heating oil. Higher prices for those products meant Chevron’s quarterly refinery profit was six times as big in 2026, despite processing less crude and selling less products.
“The return on refining, on a percentage basis, has skyrocketed,” Seng said. “Oil right now is priced what it is priced because of the Iran war. But in the meantime, the refineries are making money hand over fist.”
The global refining market is under-supplied, and with countries such as Russia and China no longer exporting, companies like Exxon and Chevron have to pick it up, said Rob Thummel, senior portfolio manager at Tortoise Capital. “The world is going to be short jet fuel, diesel and gasoline, so we’ll probably continue to see higher profits there.”
Globally, not all refineries have been able to get the supply of crude oil they need to meet demand since the conflict began, said Timothy Fitzgerald, a University of Tennessee professor of business economics who studies the petroleum industry.
As a result, refineries that have ample oil to work with, including those in the U.S., are turning high profits, particularly when they make jet fuel and diesel, which is priced about 41% higher in the U.S. than before the Strait of Hormuz was blocked.
“If you’re a company that owns a bunch of refinery capacity, things look pretty good,” Fitzgerald said.
American refineries are running at near-full capacity and poised to benefit because some refineries in the Middle East and Russia were damaged. And Asia can’t get the amount of Middle East oil needed for refining.
“Ultimately, users of the energy services pay,” Fitzgerald said. “Consumers, people like you and me buying retail motor gasoline or diesel fuel or airplane tickets. But it also means that almost everything else we buy has an embedded energy content to it ... and this is where you start to worry about it driving increases in costs.”
In the present geopolitical environment, some companies are winners while others are losers, Fitzgerald said.
“If you’re a company like a U.S. (oil) producer, even a U.S.-based international company like an Exxon or Chevron who’s got lots of production outside the Gulf, things are good. You’re selling your product at a higher price,” he said.
But companies in the Middle East that are not able to benefit from higher prices because they are struggling to get their liquefied natural gas out of the Persian Gulf or have a lot of damaged oil fields or processing facilities have a very different take on recent events, Fitzgerald added.
“Your ability to sell anything and the volume that you may be getting out is so curtailed that your revenues are way down and you’re incurring higher transportation costs and security costs,” he said.
Exxon and Chevron weren’t as profitable in the first quarter due to the way oil is traded; the first real opportunity they had to take advantage of higher prices oil was in April. Companies that had a lot of oil stored in floating tankers and available for spot-market trading, including some European ones, were able to benefit from March’s higher oil prices, Seng said.

item.title: 一枚废弃的 SpaceX 火箭正在与月球高速碰撞
item.description:
佛罗里达州卡纳维拉尔角（美联社）——一年多前发射了一对月球着陆器后，一枚漂浮的 SpaceX 火箭正在与月球相撞。
火箭的上级将于周三无意中撞向月球，在月球上留下一个陨石坑，并扬起一缕灰尘和碎石，科学家和天文爱好者都渴望观察到这一点。
太空追踪专家比尔·格雷预测，月球阳光照射下的西缘爱因斯坦陨石坑附近会发生 5,400 英里/小时（8,700 公里/小时）的撞击，是音速的七倍。由于活动在凌晨进行，美国东部和加拿大以及南美大部分地区应该能看到最好的景色。
虽然科学家们并不太关心这块特殊的太空垃圾，但它凸显了随着越来越多的物体挤入轨道，威胁日益严重。
“那里的情况变得越来越拥挤，”格雷说，他计划从加拿大新不伦瑞克省查看后果。
SpaceX 从来没有打算登陆月球。但太空专家表示，如果上级被推入绕太阳轨道，坠机事件是可以避免的。
这将是已知的第二枚因意外坠入月球而死亡的火箭。2022年，中国的一枚火箭在月球背面挖出了一对陨石坑。
对于天文学家来说幸运的是，即将到来的撞击将发生在月球近侧，其能量相当于三吨 TNT 炸药。
专家表示，撞击闪光持续时间不到一秒，可能会因为太暗而无法看到。但喷射出的物质流可能会延伸到太空几英里（公里），并且望远镜可以看到数十分钟。
洛斯阿拉莫斯国家实验室的本杰明·费尔南多说：“月球上的重力很低，没有风可以吹走灰尘。”他鼓励专业人士和业余爱好者进行观测。
他在一封电子邮件中补充道：“我们对这一事件感兴趣的部分原因是想弄清楚碎片撞击对未来宇航员造成了多大的危害。”
费尔南多预计撞击坑宽近 90 英尺，深 16 英尺（宽 27 米，深 5 米），太小，从地球上看不到，但航天器可以看到。
美国宇航局的月球勘测轨道飞行器和韩国的 Danuri 月球轨道飞行器将收集坠机现场前后的照片。费尔南多和他的团队表示，在撞击前两分钟，达努里将偏离 SpaceX 火箭一两英里（几公里）的范围。
废弃的火箭部分长约 40 英尺（12 米），重约 10,000 磅（4,500 公斤），于 2025 年 1 月 15 日吊起了两架私人月球着陆器。
其中之一——萤火虫航空航天公司的“蓝色幽灵”——成为第一艘完全成功着陆月球的私人航天器。另一个是日本 ispace 的着陆器失事。
科学家们表示，由于流星体和其他自然物体在撞击月球之前几乎不会发出任何警告，因此通过观察像即将出现的人造物体那样的精心跟踪的撞击，可以学到很多东西。美国宇航局在阿波罗时代将火箭部件和登月舱扔进月球进行地震测量。几十年后的 2009 年，NASA 故意使 LCROSS 航天器和上部级坠毁，以在月球南极附近寻找冰。
科学家表示，随着月球成为新的旅行热点，在机器人和宇航员抵达之前改善碎片监测和交通控制至关重要。
美国和中国正在竞相在未来几年内将宇航员送上月球。埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 的 SpaceX 和杰夫·贝佐斯 (Jeff Bezos) 的蓝色起源 (Blue Origin) 正在争夺为 NASA 尚未命名的阿耳忒弥斯 IV 号月球漫步者提供着陆器，后者将接替 12 名阿波罗宇航员在月球表面漫步。
“这种影响不会成为问题，”退休天体物理学家乔纳森·麦克道尔在一封电子邮件中说。“但在未来，如果月球上有长期基地，类似的影响将成为一个问题，我们不需要将火箭级留在这种混乱的轨道上。”
